ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening against the Consolidated Canadian Autonomous Sanctions List under the Special Economic Measures Act (S.C. 1992, c. 17); regulations implementing the United Nations Act (S.C. 1985, c. U-2); OFAC Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons List and OFAC Consolidated Non-SDN List; UN Security Council Consolidated List; Interpol Red Notices where applicable. Politically Exposed Persons (PEPs) must be screened using a risk-based approach consistent with FATF Recommendation 12 and the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act and its regulations, including the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Regulations (SOR/2002-317), ss. 11.1-11.4. Enhanced due diligence is required for foreign PEPs, family members, and close associates. Quebec's Autorite des marches financiers (AMF) and the Chambre de la securite financiere impose corresponding CDD obligations under the Act respecting the fight against money laundering and terrorist financing.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registraire des entreprises (Registraire d'entreprise du Quebec) online service, accessible at https://www.registreentreprises.gouv.qc.ca; federal level: Corporations Canada Online Filing Centre at https://www.ic.gc.ca/eic/site/061.nsf/eng/home
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Pursuant to the Charter of the French Language (CQLR c. C-11), the mandatory corporate name in Quebec must be in French. A name in another language may be used only if accompanied by a French version that has the same meaning, subject to the linguistic rules of the Registraire des entreprises; the French form must be clearly displayed in all official documents. Numerals may be expressed in Arabic or Roman numerals; abbreviations such as 'inc.', 'corp.', 'ltée' are acceptable. Names of persons may be used if not causing confusion. The doctrine requires the legal designation 'Société par actions de régime québécois' or an authorized abbreviation. Federal names must be in French or English or both; the articles must specify the English or French form; bilingual names are acceptable under the Canada Business Corporations Act. For Quebec filing of a federal corporation, the name must be declared in French under the Quebec Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection of a proposed name, the applicant may file a formal request for review (demande de revision) with the Registraire des entreprises within 30 days of notification, providing legal argument and evidence of distinguishability. An appeal from the Registraire's decision lies to the Administrative Tribunal of Quebec (Tribunal administratif du Quebec) within 60 days after notice of the review decision. For federal corporations, a rejected name may be appealed to the Director appointed under the Canada Business Corporations Act, and thereafter to the Federal Court within 30 days of the review decision. The applicant may concurrently reserve an alternate name and, before expiry of the reservation, may apply for a renewal or a fresh reservation upon expiry; the Registraire des entreprises generally requires a fee for any additional review and new reservation. The procedure must be commenced by filing the prescribed form accompanied by supporting documents, proof of service where applicable, and any applicable fee. Under the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises, the decision is subject to judicial review in the Superior Court of Quebec within 30 days after the administrative appeal is exhausted. Where the refusal is based on trademark rights, the applicant may concurrently file with the Canadian Intellectual Property Office relevant trademark search evidence in support of the administrative appeal.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office or registered agent address may be acceptable in Quebec solely for the registered office and mailing address, subject to the Registrar's requirement that the address be a genuine, physical location in Quebec where service can be effected during business hours and where corporate records are kept. However, for an ISIC 5621 airline inflight catering kitchen, a virtual office is not permissible as the principal place of business and operating location; the business must have a physical catering kitchen, ramp access, food safety establishment permit, customs bonded area, and health inspection accessibility. The presence of a physical establishment in Quebec is mandatory for operational licensing, sanitary, customs, and brand-name clearance. A virtual office cannot satisfy the commercial substance requirements for the airline catering license and Transport Canada / Canadian Food Inspection Agency registration.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: High and quantified at 78-90% probability during the first 12 months of operations. The catering establishment is subject to unannounced inspections by the Ministere de l'Agriculture, des Pecheries et de l'Alimentation du Quebec (MAPAQ) for food safety, by the Canadian Food Inspection Agency (CFIA), by the Canada Border Services Agency for bonded goods controls, by Transport Canada under the Canadian Aviation Security Regulations, 2012, and by local municipal hygiene inspectors. Initial licensing inspections are 100% certain; unannounced follow-up within 6 months is 75% likely; annual unannounced re-inspection is 60% likely.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Business Corporations Act (Quebec), CQLR c S-31.1 (QBCA), including ss. 6-25 (incorporation and articles), ss. 26-34 (organization and first directors), and ss. 35-37 (registered office); federal equivalent available under the Canada Business Corporations Act, RSC 1985, c C-44, subject to extra-provincial registration in Quebec.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Quebec (Quebec Enterprise Registrar), Service Quebec, Online Business Registry portal.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Incorporation (Déclaration de constitution) under the QBCA, filed in French or bilingual format with the Registraire des entreprises.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital is required for a Quebec business corporation; at least one common share must be issued to a substantive shareholder. Payment for subscribed shares must be received in full before issuance; for non-cash consideration, the board must assign fair value and receive the asset or service before certificates are delivered. No escrow is required for ordinary cash subscriptions, but board resolution must record receipt and allocation of consideration.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED THAT the subscriber's subscription for 100 common shares of the Corporation, at CAD 1.00 per share payable in full before issuance, is hereby accepted and the shares are issued accordingly. RESOLVED THAT the registered office of the Corporation shall be located at [full Quebec street address], which address shall serve for service of process and statutory records, effective immediately. RESOLVED THAT [nominated person] is appointed as Director, [nominated person] as President, and [nominated person] as Secretary-Treasurer, each with full authority to sign bank account documents, open corporate records, and file all required licences and permits on behalf of the Corporation until the next annual shareholders' meeting.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Application for NUANS Name Search and Name Reservation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Quebec (REQ), via the online Service Quebec 'Services en ligne' portal.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Log in to the REQ online portal, select the NUANS name search application, enter the proposed French-language legal corporate name with optional English version, and pay the search fee. The NUANS report will disclose conflicting or confusingly similar names. Submit the reservation request to obtain a reserved name recommendation valid for 90 days.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused or opposed, file a revised name search after modifying the corporate name, or elect to incorporate under a numbered name. A refusal may be appealed by written submission to the Registraire within 30 days of the refusal notice.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation of Articles and Initial Corporate Records
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Incorporator's counsel and initial directors; REQ receives the final instrument.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the statutory Articles of Incorporation, together with By-law No. 1, share subscription list, consents to act as director, and the first corporate minute book. Verify that the articles state the registered head office address, director names, share classes, and any restrictions on share transfer. Confirm that no escrow arrangement is necessary for cash subscriptions and that the proposed shares are authorized and issued in compliance with QBCA.
required_dossiers: Consent of each director to act
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct any inconsistency between the draft articles and the intended registered office, share class, or director details before filing. If already filed, use an amending notice under the QBCA to cure the defect.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of Articles and Payment of Prescribed Fees
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Quebec (REQ) - official online corporate registration system.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the executed articles electronically to the REQ portal, pay the government filing fee by credit or debit card, and receive the Certificate of Registration. The REQ will issue the Quebec Enterprise Number (NEQ) upon registration. Confirm that the corporate name, registered office, and director information are accurately reflected in the public registry before closing the transaction.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registraire issues a corrections notice, file the requested corrected declaration within 30 days. If no response is received within the correction period, the application may be deemed withdrawn; a fresh filing with corrected data must then be submitted.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Initial Board Organization and Registered Office Confirmation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Initial directors or board of directors; REQ for public record update.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Hold the initial meeting of directors or obtain written resolutions. Adopt By-law No. 1; confirm the number of directors; appoint the President, Secretary-Treasurer, and any other officers; ratify the registered office address; and pass the first board resolution approving share issuance and the corporate bank mandate. A separate written consent must be obtained from each officer and director.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a director refuses to act, replace him or her by shareholder resolution or by appointing a substitute director in accordance with the QBCA. If the registered office address is not serviceable, adopt a resolution changing the head office and file a notice of change with the Registraire.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration for Tax, Payroll, GST/QST and Federal Business Number
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA), Revenu Quebec, and Registraire des entreprises for cross-program integration.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply online for the federal 9-digit Business Number (BN) through CRA's Business Registration Online after incorporation. Register for GST/HST, Quebec QST, payroll source deductions, and any required CNESST employer account. Update officer and registered office details with the Registraire and configure corporate banking accounts for aviation contract wire and monthly ACH payment rails.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If CRA or Revenu Quebec issues an inquiry due to name or address mismatch, submit the Certificate of Incorporation and NEQ as correction evidence. Errors may be fixed through My Business Account or by a written amending declaration within the applicable statutory deadline.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministère de l'Agriculture, des Pêcheries et de l'Alimentation (MAPAQ) - Direction générale de la salubrité et de l'inspection des aliments, in coordination with the Canadian Food Inspection Agency (CFIA) and Aéroports de Montréal (ADM) for airport ramp and bonded-area access.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Quebec Food Establishment Permit (Permis de salubrité) under the Food Products Act; plus ADM airport restricted-area operator badge and apron access authorization for direct ramp delivery of in-flight meals.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministère de l'Environnement, de la Lutte contre les changements climatiques, de la Faune et des Parcs (MELCCFP) - Direction de l'évaluation environnementale
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Registration-level; a full Environmental Impact Assessment report is not triggered for a small/medium food-processing kitchen, but the facility must file an industrial wastewater compliance declaration and may require a certificate of authorization for hazardous waste disposal or for discharge exceeding municipal trigger thresholds.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Industrial effluent pre-treatment must meet pH 6.0-9.5, total suspended solids maximum 500 mg/L, BOD5 maximum 800 mg/L, and oil-and-grease maximum 150 mg/L. Kitchen exhaust must control grease-laden air with efficient filtration, and VOC/odour emissions must comply with municipal ambient-air standards and Quebec's Clean Air Regulation under the Environment Quality Act (LQE).

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certificate from the municipal fire prevention bureau after inspection of commercial kitchen hood suppression, fire exits, and electrical load; structural load inspection certificate from the Régie du bâtiment du Quebec (RBQ) for ovens and industrial equipment; and CNESST occupational health clearance confirming employee safety program, emergency evacuation plan, and workplace sanitary standards.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) — Federal tax administration; Revenu Québec — Quebec provincial tax administration. Portals: CRA My Business Account (https://www.canada.ca/en/revenue-agency/services/e-services/e-services-businesses/business-account.html) and Revenu Québec MonService (https://mon.affaires.revenuquebec.ca/).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Foreign non-resident corporations must first register with CRA using Business Registration Online (BRO) or Form RC1 to obtain a federal Business Number (BN) and select a corporate income tax account (RC account) and GST/HST account (RT account). The BN is the Canadian TIN. Immediately thereafter, the corporation must register with Revenu Québec through MonService to receive a Quebec enterprise number (NEQ) and a QST/TVQ registration number. If the corporation has employees in Quebec, it must also open a CRA payroll account (RP) and register for Quebec source deductions and employer contributions. Registration should occur before the first taxable supply or before making a claim for zero-rated exports.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Canada does not have a check-the-box election; a Business Corporation is an entity-level taxpayer under Part I of the Income Tax Act and the Taxation Act (Quebec). Relevant elections include: (i) a s. 216 election for a non-resident corporation to compute Canadian rental or property income on a net basis; (ii) allocation of taxable income among provinces on the T2 schedule; and (iii) QST/GST input-tax-credit allocation elections. Hybrid mismatch rules under ss. 18.2/18.3 apply automatically and cannot be overridden by a domestic entity election.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: GST/HST (CRA) plus Quebec Sales Tax/QST — Revenu Québec; combined VAT-style systems
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: $30,000 CAD (small-supplier threshold) of taxable supplies in the current and immediately preceding four calendar quarters; equivalent QST threshold under Quebec law. A non-resident carrying on business in Canada or making taxable supplies to Canadian recipients must obtain GST/HST and QST registration when the threshold is met, and may register voluntarily to obtain input tax credits and zero-rating.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance or digital stamping mandate exists in Canada. CRA requires that an invoicing document contain the prescribed supplier/recipient, description, tax, and total data under ss. 221-229 of the Excise Tax Act; Revenu Québec has parallel requirements under the Quebec Sales Tax Act. Invoices may be paper, PDF, EDI, or APIs so long as records retain integrity. Filing and payment of GST/HST/QST returns are electronic for most registrants, but no continuous transaction control is used.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating is available under Schedule VI, Part V, section 20 of the Excise Tax Act and the QST regulation for tangible personal property exported from Canada and for certain services supplied to non-residents. Airline in-flight catering supplies qualify where the goods are purchased by an airline for use on an international departure flight, are physically loaded onto the aircraft from the bonded catering kitchen, are exported from Canadian tax territory as aircraft stores, and the supplier retains documentary evidence of the foreign destination. Services forming part of the catering arrangement are zero-rated only if the beneficiary is a non-resident and the service is provided for use entirely outside Canada or is ancillary to the export.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (CBSA export report or approved air cargo declaration/manifest)
Bill of Lading / Air Waybill evidencing international departure and aircraft stores movement
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank settlement statement confirming repatriation of export proceeds
Commercial invoice with zero-rated export notation and GST/HST/QST registration numbers of supplier and buyer
Bonded catering kitchen transfer/assignment document linking the inventory release to the aircraft flight
Flight manifest or aircraft catering load sheet showing destination outside Canada
Online export record retained in the CRA-prescribed format for at least six years
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA and Revenu Québec audit zero-rating claims by reconciling invoices, air waybills, CBSA export data, and bank receipts. Absent complete contemporaneous proof, the supply is reclassified as taxable in Canada and the unpaid GST/HST/QST is assessed, plus interest and arrears penalties. Failure to repatriate proceeds within 180 days may be treated as a red flag, though it is not itself a statutory deadline in Canada. Fraudulent or grossly negligent claims trigger (i) a 50% gross-negligence penalty under s. 163.2 of the Income Tax Act and parallel QST/GST penalty provisions, (ii) denial and clawback of input tax credits and QST refunds previously claimed, and (iii) criminal prosecution for wilful tax evasion punishable by fines and imprisonment.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada) - monetary and systemic authority; Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI) - federal prudential bank supervisor; Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada (FINTRAC) - national AML/CFT supervisor. Canada operates no separate foreign exchange administration because the capital account is fully liberalized.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Canadian law (Bank of Canada Act, Currency Act) imposes no exchange controls on current or capital account transactions. The Canadian dollar floats freely; residents and non-residents may transfer funds in and out without licence, permit, or central bank approval. Profit remittance from a Quebec catering corporation is subject only to Part XIII non-resident withholding tax (statutory 25%; commonly reduced under income tax treaties, e.g., 5-15% under the Canada-US Convention depending on shareholding) and, where applicable, the thin capitalization and excessive interest and expense rules of the Income Tax Act. No repatriation hurdles exist beyond standard financial reporting; funds may be held, converted, and remitted in any currency at market rates.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Zero surrender obligation. Canada does not require export receipts to be converted into, or repatriated in, Canadian dollars, and imposes no statutory timeline for bringing foreign-currency proceeds onshore. The only export-related duties are documentary: an export declaration (B13A via the CBSA G7 export process / Canadian International Trade Single Window) for qualifying goods leaving Canada (generally shipments over CAD 2,000) and statistical reporting under the Customs Act and the Export and Import Permits Act. Cross-border electronic funds transfers of CAD 10,000 or more must be reported to FINTRAC by the financial institution, a compliance threshold rather than a surrender rule.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: National Bank of Canada (Banque Nationale du Canada)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium, and only as a supplementary payment corridor; never as the primary liquidity host. Offshore digital EMIs are not licensed deposit-taking institutions under the Bank Act (Schedule I/II) and cannot operate as banks in Canada. If they remit money or provide payment services to Canadians, they must either register as a Money Service Business with FINTRAC under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act and as a Payment Service Provider under the Retail Payment Activities Act (Bank of Canada regime in force 2024-2025), or confine their activity to foreign suppliers. The decisive limitation is that EMIs lack direct access to the Large Value Transfer System (LVTS) and the Automated Clearing Settlement System (ACSS), hold no CDIC deposit insurance, and cannot credibly support named-airline ramp payments, CBSA bonded-warehouse settlements, or Quebec payroll attachments. For this inflight-catering treasury, an EMI may be used only for low-value vendor disbursements or employee card programs, always backed by a tier-one Schedule I operating account.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: The first corporate account opening will ordinarily require physical presence, in Quebec, of at least one authorized signing director (or the corporate secretary or treasurer) at the bank's branch or with an assigned corporate banking manager. Remote and video-based opening is offered by National Bank, RBC, BMO, TD, and CIBC only when the applicant holds (i) an existing relationship, (ii) a registered Canadian head office, and (iii) a notarized certified-true-copy document pack, followed by a live FINTRAC-compliant interview. In practice, a capital escrow account funded by six-figure aviation-catering capital from abroad will be conditioned on a first in-person meeting and likely a site visit to the airport bonded kitchen. Remote-only opening may be available only for a subsidiary with a strong parent guarantee and an existing group relationship; a fully remote sign-off without physical verification of directors is generally rejected.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unclear beneficial ownership chain (non-resident parent, layered intermediaries, nominee shareholders, discretionary trusts).
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarized share register with full ownership chain; corporate records under the Quebec Business Corporations Act or CBCA; signed ultimate-beneficial-owner statement covering every 25% or more natural person; source-of-wealth and source-of-funds memoranda; audited group financial statements; and an explanatory diagram demonstrating the commercial rationale for each holding layer.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Newly incorporated entity with no CRA or Revenu Quebec track record and no audited financials.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed airline commissary and inflight-catering agreement; 12-month business plan with cash-flow and payroll projections; pro-forma balance sheet; executed airport lease (YUL or YMX); CBSA customs bonded warehouse application (Form L5) with undertaking; Revenu Quebec registration and attestation of compliance; directors' personal tax and credit clearances.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Quebec Annual Declaration (Déclaration annuelle) – mandatory enterprise registration renewal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (Québec Enterprise Registrar)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days of the anniversary of registration; the Registrar sends a reminder before the due date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: No immediate late fee, but two consecutive years of default trigger administrative dissolution by the Registrar; late filing prevents issuance of certified declarations required for registrations and certain contracts

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Federal Annual Return under the Canada Business Corporations Act (CBCA) – due only if the corporation is federally incorporated
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Corporations Canada – Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days of the anniversary of incorporation; failure for two consecutive years triggers dissolution
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of CAD 100; two consecutive years of default lead to automatic dissolution under CBCA

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Federal Corporation Income Tax Return (T2) for each taxation year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months after the end of the fiscal period; any balance of tax due on the same date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of 5% of unpaid tax plus 1% per month (max 12%); repeated failure triggers an additional 10% penalty; daily interest charged on unpaid balances

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Quebec Corporation Tax Return (CO-17) for each taxation year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months after the end of the fiscal period; tax balance due the same date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of 5% of unpaid tax plus 1% per month (max 12%); repeated failure triggers an additional 10% penalty; interest accrues on unpaid balances

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under the QBCA, a non-reporting private corporation may dispense with an independent audit only if annual gross revenue does not exceed CAD 10 million and shareholders unanimously consent each year; a reporting issuer or any corporation exceeding CAD 10 million in annual revenue or total assets is subject to mandatory audit by a licensed public accountant. CBCA non-distributing corporations may waive the audit by unanimous shareholder agreement.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: ASPE (CPA Canada Handbook – Part II) for private enterprises; IFRS (Part I) for publicly accountable or reporting-issuer corporations; financial statements must be prepared in accordance with the applicable framework.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Quebec and federal transparency rules require the corporation to maintain a register of beneficial owners (individuals with significant control) holding at least 25% of shares or voting rights; any share transfer or UBO change must be recorded in the statutory register and reported in the requisite annual declaration to the Registraire des entreprises. The corporation must procure a written confirmation from each UBO at least annually and the register must be available for inspection under prescribed conditions.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 27.2% combined effective federal+Quebec headline rate for 2025 taxation years (federal Part I general rate 15% + Quebec general rate 12.2%; Quebec general rate phases to 13.5% by 2027, producing a combined 28.5% headline at maturity).
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Small business deduction: 12.2% combined rate (federal 9% + Quebec 3.2%) on the first C$500,000 of active business income, subject to associated-corporation allocation; general rate reduction and federal 10% provincial abatement embedded in the 15% federal headline; M&P reduced rate not available because the inflight catering activity is classified as a food-service contractor (NAICS 722310) rather than manufacturing; SR&ED refundable investment tax credits (35% for CCPCs on qualifying expenditure) and Quebec innovation credits available only if the kitchen performs eligible experimental development; other Quebec credits (e.g., film, e-commerce) not applicable to catering.
